title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has published its response to the 2020 Committee report on “Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards,” outlining how it plans to strengthen AI governance and protect public interests. It emphasises setting higher standards, improving accountability, and investing in research to ensure AI systems are safe, fair and beneficial for society.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector to maintain fairness, integrity, and quality of assessments. It responds to government requests by setting clear rules that allow technology to support learning while protecting the validity and security of exams.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report evaluates how copyrighted material is used in AI training and the legal and ethical impacts of that practice. It examines potential risks and suggests guidelines to balance innovation with respect for intellectual property rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, recognising that stronger oversight and action are needed to manage the risks and opportunities of artificial intelligence. It pledges to strengthen regulation, support ethical AI development, encourage innovation, and ensure that the benefits of AI are shared fairly while protecting public interests.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee that will examine how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards, detailing its objectives and how it will operate. It also includes a FAQ section that explains key points and answers common questions for stakeholders.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into how artificial intelligence should be governed. The submission likely outlines the organization’s views and recommendations on policies, oversight, and best practices for responsible AI deployment.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how AI technologies influence the oversight of medical products, focusing on safety, efficacy, and compliance with regulatory frameworks. It outlines steps for implementing the AI White Paper principles to ensure responsible AI integration in healthcare product regulation.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑enabled defence force in the world for its size. It outlines how advanced AI will be integrated into operations and decision‑making to achieve this leadership position.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to seize opportunities offered by AI. It also describes measures to manage and mitigate the potential risks associated with adopting AI technologies in transportation.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report details how copyright‑protected works are being used to train and improve AI systems, focusing on compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It reviews current practices, identifies legal and technical challenges, and offers recommendations for balancing innovation with copyright protection.
